questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify the homologous series to which A, B and C each belong.

A: ........

B: ........

C: ........ *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
- **A**, $\mathrm{C_2H_6}$ (ethane), fits the general formula $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}$: it belongs to the **alkanes**.
- **B**, $\mathrm{C_3H_7OH}$ (propanol), contains the $-\mathrm{OH}$ group: it belongs to the **alcohols** (general formula $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}OH}$).
- **C**, $\mathrm{C_2H_4}$ (ethene), fits $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n}}$ and has a carbon-carbon double bond: it belongs to the **alkenes**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define isomerism.

(ii) Suggest which of the compounds will exhibit isomerism.

(iii) Draw two structures of the isomers in b(ii). *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Isomerism** is the existence of two or more compounds that have the **same molecular formula but different structural formulae** (a different arrangement of the atoms in the molecule). The compounds are called isomers.

(ii) **B**, $\mathrm{C_3H_7OH}$, shows isomerism. (Ethane and ethene have no isomers.) The $-\mathrm{OH}$ group can be fixed to different carbon atoms of the chain.

(iii) Two isomers of $\mathrm{C_3H_7OH}$ (molecular formula $\mathrm{C_3H_8O}$ for both):

- **Propan-1-ol**: $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-OH}$ (the $-\mathrm{OH}$ group is on the end carbon atom);
- **Propan-2-ol**: $\mathrm{CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_3}$ (the $-\mathrm{OH}$ group is on the middle carbon atom).

In the answer, each structure is drawn in full, showing all the atoms and all the bonds: a chain of three carbon atoms, each with single bonds to hydrogen atoms, and the O-H group attached to carbon 1 in the first isomer and to carbon 2 in the second.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Write an equation, stating reaction condition, for the conversion of C to A.

Equation: ........

Reaction condition: ........ *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Ethene (C) is converted to ethane (A) by **hydrogenation**, the addition of hydrogen across the double bond:

$$
\mathrm{C_2H_4 + H_2 \rightarrow C_2H_6}
$$

Check: C 2 = 2; H 4 + 2 = 6.

**Reaction condition:** a **nickel catalyst** at about **150 $^\circ$C** (platinum or palladium also work).

questions.enonce_markdown: Describe a simple chemical test for B. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
B is an alcohol. **Test:** warm a little of B with **acidified potassium dichromate(VI) solution**. The colour changes from **orange to green** because the alcohol is oxidised.

(Another simple test: add a small piece of sodium; the colourless gas given off, hydrogen, burns with a 'pop'. This test is less specific, since water and acids also react with sodium.)
